name: An Adjacent Support-Four Corner Can Repair a Prescribed Endpoint
statement: There is a 289-concept rooted factor $(B,29)$ and an ample one-concept extension $M=B\cup\{157\}$ acquiring four directions such that both $29$ and $157$ are adjacent corners of the completed four-cube and $M$ peels to either one, while deleting the nonroot corner $157$ returns $B$, which cannot peel to $29$. Thus even deletion of a corner adjacent to the root can destroy the prescribed endpoint; support size at most two cannot do so, while support four can.
proof: The certified addition has acquired support $\{1,2,7,8\}$ and makes both endpoints corners joined in direction $7$. Stored corner orders end at each marked vertex. Deleting the new vertex exactly recovers the certified rooted factor, whose root-ending peeling is impossible. The low-support extension theorem supplies the contrasting impossibility through support two.
